AfterObtained.issue: Confirms the record's G2 analysis (reward-options hooks dropped) and its liveness (LIVE but rare — ~1 in 20,000 Neow's Bones picks). Fixed by routing after_obtained's Uniform-Rare draw through the shared create_reward_cards (mutate_pity=False, is_card_reward=False, extra_flags=NO_UPGRADE_ROLL) instead of a hand-rolled pick loop, restoring both Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions[Late] passes. G1 (pool source) and G3 (skippable) were already faithful and are re-confirmed by test_hefty_tablet_offer_is_all_rare / test_hefty_tablet_obtain_purpose_is_ still_skippable (the latter in test_r13_relic2.py, untouched, still green). Replaces the reasoning in test_r13_relic2.py's test_hefty_tablet_after_obtained_never_calls_modify_card_reward_options, which pinned the pre-fix (buggy) behavior as correct — see this report's Findings §1; that test is outside this lane's footprint and needs a follow-up edit/delete.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the port builds its Rare candidates with cards.pool.pool_card_ids() -- the FilterForCombat pool -- where CardFactory.CreateForReward draws from CardPool.GetUnlockedCards(), so two Rare cards are unreachable and every draw indexes a shorter list
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The candidates come from the REWARD pool. HeftyTablet.cs:29 goes through CardFactory.CreateForReward, whose candidate set is `options.GetPossibleCards(player).Except(blacklist)` (CardFactory.cs:214-217) = `CardPools.SelectMany(p => p.GetUnlockedCards(...)).Where(CardPoolFilter)` (CardCreationOptions.cs:168-178); there is NO FilterForCombat anywhere on that path and the Uniform arm only drops Basic and Ancient (CardFactory.cs:221-224). relics/hefty_tablet.py now calls `reward_pool_card_ids(pool=run.card_pool)`, the helper cards/pool.py already had for exactly this path and whose docstring names the two casualties, in place of `pool_card_ids()` (the FilterForCombat mirror). EXECUTED: the Rare candidate set difference between the two helpers is exactly {'feed', 'not_yet'} -- both RARE with can_be_generated_in_combat False -- and over 40 seeds the relic's offers now include them, where before they were unreachable on every seed. The second observable closes with it: NextItem indexes into the candidate list in pool order, so a 23-item list returned a different card than the game's 25-item list for the same draw, and all three offers diverged. Same root cause as the batch-2 bowlbug finding ('reward pool = full GetUnlockedCards not FilterForCombat'), at a relic site.  Pinned by test/test_relic_live_tail.py.  NOT CLOSED: nothing at this site.  The text it replaced read: MECHANISM: HeftyTablet.cs:29 builds `new CardCreationOptions(Owner.Character.CardPool, ..., CardRarityOddsType.Uniform, c => c.Rarity == CardRarity.Rare)`, and CardFactory.CreateForReward -> CreateForReward(player, blacklist, options) resolves the candidate set as `options.GetPossibleCards(player).Except(blacklist)` (CardFactory.cs:214-217), where GetPossibleCards is `CardPools.SelectMany(p => p.GetUnlockedCards(...)).Where(CardPoolFilter)` (CardCreationOptions.cs:168-178). There is NO FilterForCombat anywhere on that path -- the Uniform arm only drops Basic and Ancient (CardFactory.cs:221-224). hefty_tablet.py:20-25 uses pool_card_ids(), which cards/pool.py:100-117 documents as the FilterForCombat mirror and which drops every card with can_be_generated_in_combat = False. The sim already HAS the right helper: cards/pool.py:120-131's reward_pool_card_ids exists for exactly this path and its docstring names the two casualties. LIVE, no dormancy question, executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py tablet-pool): the port's Rare candidate list is 23 entries and the game's is 25; the two missing are `feed` and `not_yet`, both rarity RARE with can_be_generated_in_combat = False. Two observables, not one: Feed and Not Yet -- a max-HP scaler and a revive, i.e. two of the strongest Rares in the pool -- can never be offered by Hefty Tablet in the sim, AND because Rng.NextItem indexes into the candidate list in pool order, a 23-item list returns a DIFFERENT card than a 25-item list for the same draw, so all three offered cards diverge on every seed. Both sides ported and obtainable: Hefty Tablet is offered by the ported Neow event (events/neow.py; Neow.cs:99 `RelicOption<HeftyTablet>` on the CURSED branch). Same root cause as the batch-2 finding recorded in the project's own notes for the bowlbug fight ('reward pool = full GetUnlockedCards not FilterForCombat, Feed/NotYet offerable') -- this is that shape at a relic site. Rule 7: CardFactory.cs, CardCreationOptions.cs, cards/pool.py and events/neow.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): CardFactory.CreateForReward runs Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions on the three cards unless CardCreationFlags.NoModifyHooks is set, and HeftyTablet sets only NoUpgradeRoll -- the port calls no such hook
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardFactory.cs:104-107 folds `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions(player.RunState, player, list2, options, out modifiers)` and then AfterModifyingCardRewardOptions over the created reward list; HeftyTablet.cs:29 sets `WithFlags(CardCreationFlags.NoUpgradeRoll)` and nothing else, so the modify hooks DO run for this relic's three cards. hefty_tablet.py:17-42 builds the options with make_card and hands them straight to run.select_cards, never touching the sim's `modify_card_reward_options` -- which exists on the base class (relics/base.py:172-176) and is implemented by four ported relics (executed, py audit/tools/relic_probes_b07.py tablet-pool: relics/_eggs.py, relics/glitter.py, relics/silken_tress.py, relics/silver_crucible.py). So in the game Silver Crucible would upgrade Hefty Tablet's three Rares and Silken Tress would enchant one; in the sim it does neither. DORMANT, and the reachability argument is specific rather than assumed: Hefty Tablet's ONLY ported grant path is Neow (executed by probe `pool`: bag=-, granted_by=events/neow.py), which is floor 0, where the player holds nothing but the character's starting relic -- so no card-reward-modifying relic can be held when this AfterObtained runs. It is not in any grab bag on either side (the C# EventRelicPool that lists it is a registry with no random puller -- executed: `grep -rn EventRelicPool src/ --include=*.cs` outside its own file returns only the AbstractModelSubtypes type table and ModelDb's registration). CONCRETE UNPORTED THING that makes it live: any source that grants Hefty Tablet after floor 0 -- an Event-rarity relic reward, a shrine option, or a shop slot. Note the contrast with relic/kaleidoscope in this batch, which DOES set NoCardPoolModifications and so correctly expects no modification. Rule 7: CardFactory.cs, relics/base.py, relics/_eggs.py, relics/silken_tress.py, relics/silver_crucible.py and events/neow.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G3: `CardSelectCmd.FromChooseACardScreen(..., canSkip: true)` (HeftyTablet.cs:32) may return null -- the player can decline all three. RE-DERIVED 2026-07-26: the sim can decline too
guards.rationale: CORRECTED by the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass; the previous entry's premise was FALSE and its deliberate-divergence verdict rested entirely on it. It said `run.select_cards(purpose, candidates, 1)` 'has no skip channel at all'. sts2_rl/relics/hefty_tablet.py:40 passes purpose="obtain", and "obtain" IS one of the three members of `sts2_rl/driver.py:77 SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES`. THE DISCRIMINATOR, settled by the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass and applied at every relic card-selection site: the sim CAN model a decline exactly when the purpose string is in `sts2_rl/driver.py:77 SKIPPABLE_PURPOSES` (`card_reward`, `obtain`, `transform_optional`). For those, `RunDriver._card_selector` (sts2_rl/driver.py:246-267) issues a real DecisionRequest whose `legal_actions()` appends the skip index (sts2_rl/driver.py:154-158) and breaks out on it; for every other purpose it either short-circuits at sts2_rl/driver.py:249 (`count >= len(remaining)`) or runs the loop with no skip action, so exactly `count` cards come back. EXECUTED: driving `RunDriver._card_selector` with an `_ask` that raises, purpose 'gambling_chip' / candidates ['a','b','c'] / count 3 RETURNS ['a','b','c'] without ever asking, while 'card_reward', 'obtain' and 'transform_optional' each raise, i.e. each really does ask. The C# side of the test is `CardSelectorPrefs`: the 2-argument constructor (CardSelectorPrefs.cs:63-67) is `this(prompt, selectCount, selectCount)`, so MinSelect == MaxSelect and the screen is FORCED, while a MinSelect of 0 or an explicit `canSkip: true` makes it declinable (`canSkip` DEFAULTS to false, CardSelectCmd.cs:216). So HeftyTablet's `canSkip: true` screen and the sim's "obtain" selection agree: both let the player leave with the Injury and no Rare, and `for card in run.select_cards(...)` over an empty return adds nothing (sts2_rl/run.py:384-390 honours it). Matches relic/lead_paperweight guard N4, which reached the same conclusion for the same reason at the other `canSkip: true` relic screen (binding rule 3). The no-selector default (`run.rng.sample`, sts2_rl/run.py:390) always picks one, but that is a default POLICY, not a modelling limit -- lead_paperweight N4 says the same. Rule 7: sts2_rl/driver.py, sts2_rl/run.py and audit/records/relic/lead_paperweight.json are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N1: `CardRarityOddsType.Uniform` + `WithFlags(CardCreationFlags.NoUpgradeRoll)` (HeftyTablet.cs:29) -- what the port's Rewards-stream loop has to reproduce
guards.rationale: Three separate clauses, all matched. (a) Uniform means NO rarity roll: CardFactory.cs:221-224 takes the whole predicate-filtered set minus Basic/Ancient rather than calling RollForRarity, so the three cards cost no rarity draws. (b) One `rng.NextItem(items)` per card on `player.PlayerRng.Rewards` (CardFactory.cs:235-236), with the accumulating blacklist `Except(blacklist)` at line 217 making the picks distinct -- hefty_tablet.py:30-37 does exactly that, `run.player_rng.rewards.next_item(pool)` followed by `pool.remove(cid)`, three times. (c) NoUpgradeRoll skips the RollForUpgrade draw at CardFactory.cs:98-102, so no upgrade-stream draws happen either and the offered cards are un-upgraded; the port never upgrades. The parity gate `if run.rng_set is not None` selects that path and falls back to a plain random.sample in legacy mode, which is the sim's standing legacy/parity split rather than a divergence. Rule 7: CardFactory.cs and sts2_rl/run.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N2: the candidate pool is `base.Owner.Character.CardPool` ONLY -- the Ironclad pool, with no Colorless and no Curse pool
guards.rationale: HeftyTablet.cs:29 passes a single-element pool list built from the character's own pool, and hefty_tablet.py:22-25 defaults pool_card_ids() to IRONCLAD_POOL (cards/pool.py:102). Recorded because several other reward paths in the game DO add the Colorless pool, and including it here would change both the offered cards and the list length that G1's RNG draw indexes into. Rule 7: cards/pool.py is not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N3: the ORDER and POSITION of the two deck additions -- chosen card first, Injury second, both appended at the deck's end
guards.rationale: HeftyTablet.cs:33-38 builds `[Injury]`, inserts the chosen card at index 0, and passes the whole list to ONE `CardPileCmd.Add(list, PileType.Deck)`; hefty_tablet.py:40-42 adds the chosen card then the Injury through two run.add_card calls. Same resulting order, and both append at the end, which is the position CardCmd.cs:437 pins for out-of-combat additions (PROMPT.md bug class 8). The batched-vs-sequential difference is not observable: run.add_card runs modify_card_being_added_to_deck before each append and after_card_added_to_deck after it, which is per-card in C# too. The Injury curse is ported (cards/pool.py's CURSE_POOL lists `injury`). Rule 7: CardCmd.cs, sts2_rl/run.py and cards/pool.py are not hashed by this record.

guards.what: N4: `count = min(self.CARDS, len(rares))` (hefty_tablet.py:26) -- a defensive clamp C# does not have
guards.rationale: C# would throw from CreateForReward if the pool ran dry (CardFactory.cs:237-240 raises InvalidOperationException on a null pick). The clamp cannot bind with today's content -- executed (probe tablet-pool): 23 Rare candidates against CardsVar(3) -- so it is unreachable defensive code rather than a divergence. Recorded because a shrinking pool is the shape in which a clamp silently hides a real problem, and here the number to watch is 23 vs 3.

guards.rationale: No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so 3 is the pinned non-ascension value.
